question: Valabhi type of Nagara temples are generally __________ in shape, with a roof that rises into a vaulted chamber.
solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Valabhi type of Nagara temples are characterized by their **rectangular shape**.
 
• These temples feature a roof that rises into a **vaulted chamber**.
 
• The architectural style is distinct within the Nagara temple architecture, which is prominent in northern India.
 
• The Valabhi type is one of several sub-styles within the broader Nagara architecture, each having unique structural elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara Architecture**:

 
 
• A prominent temple architecture style in northern India characterized by its beehive-shaped tower called Shikhara.
 
• Often built on a raised platform called Jagati.
 
 
 
• **Sub-Styles of Nagara**:
 
 
• Rekha-Prasad: Features a linear tower.
 
• Phamsana: Characterized by a broader base and shorter height.
 
• Valabhi: Recognized by its rectangular shape with a vaulted roof.
 
 
 
• **Temple Components**:
 
 
• Garbhagriha: The innermost sanctum where the deity resides.
 
• Mandapa: The entrance hall.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations**:
 
 
• The Nagara style varies significantly across different regions in terms of structural design and ornamentation.
